resource.name: Lenny AMA (always fresh)
resource.description: The catch-all front door: a single question box that answers any product / growth / strategy / hiring / career / leadership question (or any general question where a product lens is useful) from the current corpus synthesis, in a PM lens. The only corpus-wide tool in the bundle. Always fresh in two senses: it reads the live knowledge base at answer time, and it sweeps the obsolete + cautions layers so the answer flags when older advice has decayed or drew strong audience pushback. Names its sources, ends with a concrete next step, and offers the right specific tool when the question maps to one. No state, no scoring. The UI is an optional question box; the tool is question-in/answer-out and works chat-natively.

tools.name: ama_ask
tools.description: MUST CALL whenever the user asks any product, growth, strategy, hiring, career, or leadership question, or any general question where a product-thinking lens is the useful one (prioritizing across competing asks, judging whether a metric is good, thinking through a tradeoff), AND you do not already have a more specific Working-from-Lenny app in play. This is the corpus-wide catch-all: do NOT answer such a question from your own training without calling this tool first, because the corpus is fresher and decay-aware where your training is not. Takes a free-text `question` (and optional `k` for retrieval breadth). Returns a narration_brief directly (this is a single-call Path 4 tool — it IS the narration tool; there is no separate narrate / get-pending step). Render the answer from the brief: answer directly first in a PM lens grounded in `corpus`, then — if `inputs.decay` is present — surface what changed (an obsolete claim the corpus retired, or a caution with its audience-pushback vote count) instead of repeating advice that expired, then name the sources, then give one concrete next step. If `inputs.suggested_app` is present, offer that specific app at the end (for example 'this is really a north star question, want the NSM Finder? I can open it') as a soft offer, never as a deflection from answering. Follow the brief's voice_rules.

inputs.description: Carries the user's question, the retrieved hits (each with slug + kind topic|obsolete|caution + last_updated), an optional `decay` block built from any obsolete/caution hit, and an optional `suggested_app` { id, name, entry_tool } resolved from the routing map.

corpus.description: Map of retrieved source slug to corpus chunk text (truncated), spanning topics / obsolete / cautions.

_meta.dev.workingfromlenny.comment: MCP resource spec for #54 Lenny AMA (always fresh). Phase 3 .mcpb bundle target. Architecture locked in PHASE2_BUILD.md #11 (always-fresh corpus-wide retrieval). This is the only corpus-wide tool and the only single-call Path 4 tool: `ama_ask` returns a narration_brief directly and the host renders the answer on the same turn, so there is NO score -> narrate -> get-pending spine and NO persistence (a reviewer should not expect the four-tool shape the quiz/wizard/generator apps use — AMA's single-tool shape is the deliberate #11 design). Retrieval uses a shared `retrieveAcrossCorpus(question, k)` helper added to bundle/src/lib/corpus.ts (later implementation pass), matching over knowledge/topics/ + knowledge/obsolete/ + knowledge/cautions/ and tagging each hit with kind + last_updated. Decay-aware: obsolete/caution hits flow into inputs.decay and the directive surfaces what changed / what drew pushback. Routing: inputs.suggested_app is set from the keyword->app map in authoring.md when the question maps cleanly to one app (humor apps #51/#52/#53 are intentionally not routed to). readOnlyHint: true, no sampling. The web variant is a claude.ai handoff (APP_IDEAS implementation note). Featured first on the launcher home + site (STATUS.md 4c). Tool description verbatim-matches the runtime meta.description string.

dev.workingfromlenny.catalog.one_liner: Ask anything; a current, decay-aware answer from the corpus, with sources.

dev.workingfromlenny.path_4.summary: ama_ask is a single-call Path 4 tool: it runs whole-corpus retrieval (topics + obsolete + cautions), builds the decay flags + the optional app-routing suggestion, and returns a narration_brief directly. The host renders the answer from directive + voice_rules + structure + inputs (question, retrieved hits, decay, suggested_app) + corpus (the retrieved chunks). No persistence, no sampling, no separate narrate/get-pending step.

The brief shape mirrors PitfallNarrateOutput / the other narration briefs; the retrieval set is corpus-wide rather than per-app fixed anchors.
